# rust — Rules projection

## api-surface

rust/RA-01  Every public item is documented in the Rust rustdoc style.

rust/RA-02  Keep the public surface small. `pub` is a promise, not a default.

rust/RA-03  A breaking change to a `pub` item is a major version.

## control-flow

rust/RF-01  Prefer combinators + `?`, then early returns / guards, then small private helpers.

rust/RF-02  Nesting deeper than 3–4 levels is forbidden.

rust/RF-03  Max 5 parameters per function; use a builder or config struct beyond that.

rust/RF-04  Prefer borrowing (`&T`, `&mut T`) over ownership when either works.

rust/RF-05  Match exhaustively. A `_` arm that hides a real case is a defect.

rust/RF-06  Single responsibility per function and type.

## error-handling

rust/RE-01  Every layer defines its own error enum via thiserror. Never `anyhow`.
            check: rg 'anyhow' --glob '*.rs' → 0

rust/RE-02  Cross-layer propagation uses `#[from]` / `From`; never inline `.map_err` at a call site — a call-site `.map_err` means a `From` impl is missing, add the impl.
            check: rg '\.map_err\(' --glob '*.rs' → review each hit

rust/RE-03  Never `.unwrap()` in production paths.
            check: rg '\.unwrap\(' src/ --glob '!**/tests/**' → review each hit; none outside `#[cfg(test)]`

rust/RE-04  `.expect()` only for documented invariants, with an explanatory comment.

rust/RE-05  Fallible operations return `Result<T, E>`. Propagate with `?`.

rust/RE-06  The public API boundary converts domain errors into the gateway type via `From`.

## input-parsing

rust/RP-01  Parse wire values into domain newtypes at the adapter edge. Do not validate later. Naked `String` / `&str` must not cross into the core.

rust/RP-02  Newtypes that wrap wire input are constructed at the edge, not deep in the core.

rust/RP-03  Invalid input dies at the parse boundary. The core receives a domain value or nothing.

## layering

rust/RL-01  Every function operates at one consistent level of abstraction.

rust/RL-02  Calculations are pure. Actions sit at the edges. Data is immutable.

rust/RL-03  Higher layers compose lower ones. The call graph must be obvious.

rust/RL-04  An error type stays in its layer. Crossing a boundary is a `From` conversion, not a mix-in.

rust/RL-05  A calculation about one type lives in `impl Type` when Self is monomorphic and the fn does not need late-bound lifetimes. Leave it free only when the impl would inherit unused generics or lifetimes, or a `for<'a> fn(...)` pointer is required.

## safety-performance-and-security

rust/RS-01  Never use `unsafe` without documented safety invariants and a justification.
            check: rg 'unsafe' --glob '*.rs' → review each hit

rust/RS-02  Minimize allocations: prefer `&str` / `Cow<'_, str>` over `String` when either works.

rust/RS-03  Use `Vec::with_capacity` when the size is known up front.

rust/RS-04  Prefer borrowing and channels over `Arc` / `Rc` / `Mutex` when either works.

rust/RS-05  Prefer `RwLock` over `Mutex` for read-heavy cases.

rust/RS-06  Never store secrets in source.

rust/RS-07  Configuration comes from the environment or an approved crate. Never from literals in code.

rust/RS-08  Never log passwords, tokens, or PII.

rust/RS-09  Do not trust untrusted input past the parse edge.

## testing

rust/RT-01  Unit tests cover every new calculation and public item.
            tag: test

rust/RT-02  Tests follow Arrange-Act-Assert.
            tag: test

rust/RT-03  Test code lives in `#[cfg(test)]` modules.
            tag: test

rust/RT-04  Every error path is exercised. Happy path is not enough.
            tag: test

rust/RT-05  Never commit commented-out tests.
            tag: test

rust/RT-06  Mock actions at integration edges. Never mock calculations.
            tag: test

rust/RT-07  `cargo test --workspace` is clean before the change is done.
            tag: test
            check: cargo test --workspace

## tokio-runtime

rust/RY-01  Work backward from a user-facing metric. A long poll is not a defect by itself.

rust/RY-02  Yield between immediately-ready units when the goal is multi-tenant latency. Batch the same work when the goal is throughput.

rust/RY-03  Batch filesystem and other blocking work into the largest sensible `spawn_blocking` segment. Do not sprinkle `tokio::fs` calls.
            check: rg 'tokio::fs::' --glob '*.rs' → review each hit

rust/RY-04  Do not spawn a task whose useful work is measured in microseconds.

rust/RY-05  Treat the blocking pool and the global queue as contended globals. Do not flood them from outside a worker.

rust/RY-06  Never hold a blocking mutex, `parking_lot` lock, or `RwLock` across I/O, flush, or `.await` on a Tokio worker. `tokio::sync::Mutex` only when the critical section lasts milliseconds.

rust/RY-07  Bound task fan-out with a `Semaphore`. Unbounded spawn against a downstream is a defect.

rust/RY-08  Pin Tokio workers off cores that run other processes or long non-yielding Rust threads.

rust/RY-09  Do not block inside `join!` or `select!`. There is no work-stealing inside a task.

## tooling

rust/RC-01  `cargo fmt` is clean before any change is complete.
            check: cargo fmt --all --check

rust/RC-02  `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -W clippy::pedantic -D warnings` is clean.
            check: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -W clippy::pedantic -D warnings

rust/RC-03  Never add `#[allow(clippy::too_many_*)]`. Refactor instead.

rust/RC-04  No wildcard imports except preludes or `use super::*` in tests.

rust/RC-05  Import order: `std` → approved external crates → local modules.

rust/RC-06  Prefer the standard library. A new third-party crate needs explicit user approval.

rust/RC-07  No `dbg!`, `println!`, or commented-out code in production paths.
            check: rg 'dbg!|println!' src/ → 0

rust/RC-08  `cargo build` and `cargo test` run with zero warnings.

## type-system

rust/RD-01  Use newtypes for semantically distinct values (`UserId(u64)` vs `OrderId(u64)`). Wire-originated strings are RP-01's case, not a second rule here.

rust/RD-02  Prefer `Option<T>` over sentinel values or boolean flags.

rust/RD-03  Derive `Debug`, `Clone`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash` where those traits are honest.

rust/RD-04  `#[derive(Default)]` only when a truly sensible default exists.

rust/RD-05  Treat data as immutable by default.

rust/RD-06  Use a builder for complex construction with private fields (invariants enforced in `build()`).
